clean_title: AI refutes Erdős’s unit distance conjecture, solving a famous open problem
summary:
1/ Ten months ago, I was ecstatic that AI could win IMO gold.
Today, that excitement feels quaint: an internal @OpenAI model has refuted Erdos’s unit distance conjecture—a research result that one could recommend “acceptance without any hesitation” to the Annals of Mathematics.
Quoting @OpenAI
Today, we share a breakthrough on the planar unit distance problem, a famous open question first posed by Paul Erdős in 1946.
For nearly 80 years, mathematicians believed the best possible solutions looked roughly like square grids.
An OpenAI model has now disproved that belief, discovering an entirely new family of constructions that performs better.
This marks the first time AI has autonomously solved a prominent open problem central to a field of mathematics.

Today, an internal OpenAI model has refuted Erdős’s unit distance conjecture, a famous open problem in mathematics. This result is so significant that it could be recommended for acceptance without hesitation to the Annals of Mathematics, one of the most prestigious journals. The model was tested as part of a side project to challenge the hardest problems.

The breakthrough concerns the planar unit distance problem, first posed by Paul Erdős in 1946. For nearly 80 years, mathematicians believed that the best solutions resembled square grids. The AI model discovered a completely new family of constructions that outperform these traditional solutions. This is the first time AI has autonomously solved a major open problem at the core of a mathematical field.
